UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents the portfolio owner's personal and professional information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

name.description: The full name of the portfolio owner.

email.description: The primary contact email address of the portfolio owner.

phone.description: The primary contact phone number of the portfolio owner.

bio.description: A personal biography or introductory text about the portfolio owner.

profilePictureId.description: Reference to the Image entity for the portfolio owner's profile picture. (Relationship: Image 1:1 UserProfile)

experience.description: A list of professional work experiences.

education.description: A list of educational background details.

instagramUrl.description: URL to the portfolio owner's Instagram profile.

githubUrl.description: URL to the portfolio owner's GitHub profile.

linkedinUrl.description: URL to the portfolio owner's LinkedIn profile.

Technology.title: Technology
Technology.description: Represents a skill, programming language, framework, or tool the portfolio owner is proficient in.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Technology entity.

name.description: The name of the technology or skill (e.g., 'Node.js', 'Vue.js').

category.description: The category of the technology (e.g., 'Programming Language', 'Framework', 'Database', 'Tool', 'System Analysis').

description.description: A brief description of the technology or skill.

iconUrl.description: URL to an icon representing the technology.

Project.title: Project
Project.description: Represents a portfolio project with details, links, and associated technologies and images.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Project entity.

description.description: A detailed and impactful description of the project, potentially AI-enhanced.

liveDemoUrl.description: URL to the live demonstration of the project.

repositoryUrl.description: URL to the project's code repository (e.g., GitHub).

technologyIds.description: References to Technology entities used in this project. (Relationship: Project N:N Technology)

imageIds.description: References to Image entities associated with this project for visual showcase. (Relationship: Project N:N Image)

Image.title: Image
Image.description: Represents a visual asset, such as a project screenshot, certificate image, or gallery item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Image entity.

url.description: The URL where the image is hosted.

altText.description: Alternative text for the image, used for accessibility.

description.description: A descriptive text for the image, particularly for gallery items.

uploadDate.description: The date and time when the image was uploaded.

Certificate.title: Certificate
Certificate.description: Represents a professional certification, achievement, or badge.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Certificate entity.

name.description: The name of the certificate or achievement.

issuingBody.description: The organization or institution that issued the certificate.

dateIssued.description: The date when the certificate was issued.

credentialId.description: An optional credential ID or verification code for the certificate.

certificateUrl.description: URL to the official certificate document or verification page.

imageId.description: Reference to the Image entity for a visual representation of the certificate. (Relationship: Image 1:1 Certificate)

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Represents a service offered by the portfolio owner that clients can inquire about.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Service entity.

name.description: The name of the service (e.g., 'Web Development', 'System Analysis').

description.description: A brief description of what the service entails.

HireMeInquiry.title: HireMeInquiry
HireMeInquiry.description: Represents an inquiry from a potential client interested in hiring the portfolio owner.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HireMeInquiry entity.

clientName.description: The name of the client making the inquiry.

clientEmail.description: The email address of the client.

clientPhone.description: The phone number of the client.

message.description: The client's message or detailed request.

serviceIds.description: References to Service entities the client is interested in. (Relationship: HireMeInquiry N:N Service)

budget.description: The estimated budget provided by the client (can be a range or value).

timeline.description: The estimated timeline for the project as specified by the client.

urgency.description: The urgency level of the client's request (e.g., 'low', 'medium', 'high').

cvPortfolioUrl.description: URL to the client's uploaded CV or portfolio, if provided.

submissionDate.description: The date and time when the inquiry was submitted.

isSpam.description: A flag indicating if the inquiry is detected as spam.

status.description: The current status of the inquiry (e.g., 'new', 'reviewed', 'contacted', 'rejected').

CollaborationInquiry.title: CollaborationInquiry
CollaborationInquiry.description: Represents an inquiry from a potential collaborator expressing interest in working together.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CollaborationInquiry entity.

collaboratorName.description: The name of the potential collaborator.

collaboratorEmail.description: The email address of the potential collaborator.

collaboratorPhone.description: The phone number of the potential collaborator.

projectIdea.description: A description of the project idea or area of interest for collaboration.

projectScope.description: Details about the scope of the proposed project.

estimatedTimeline.description: The estimated timeline for the collaborative project.

documentUrls.description: URLs to uploaded project documents or files provided by the collaborator.

submissionDate.description: The date and time when the collaboration inquiry was submitted.

status.description: The current status of the collaboration inquiry (e.g., 'new', 'reviewed', 'contacted', 'rejected').

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: Represents visitor comments and feedback on projects or the portfolio overall.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Comment entity.

authorName.description: The name of the person leaving the comment.

authorEmail.description: The email address of the comment author (optional).

commentText.description: The actual text content of the comment.

submissionDate.description: The date and time when the comment was submitted.

projectId.description: Reference to the Project entity if the comment is specific to a project. (Relationship: Project 1:N Comment)

isApproved.description: A flag indicating if the comment has been approved for display by the portfolio owner.

isSpam.description: A flag indicating if the comment is detected as spam.

ChatUser.title: ChatUser
ChatUser.description: Represents a user authorized to access the 'chatBRJ' feature.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ChatUser entity.

username.description: The unique username chosen by the chat user.

email.description: The email address of the chat user (optional, for account recovery).

joinDate.description: The date and time when the chat user registered.

ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description: Represents a message sent within the 'chatBRJ' feature.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ChatMessage entity.

chatUserId.description: Reference to the ChatUser who sent this message. (Relationship: ChatUser 1:N ChatMessage)

messageContent.description: The text content of the chat message.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the message was sent.

definition.description: Collection for designating administrators. Document IDs ('adminId') must match Firebase Authentication UIDs. Used for database-backed access control (DBAC) by checking document existence.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The Firebase Authentication UID of the administrator.

definition.description: The single document representing the portfolio owner's public profile information. Publicly readable, but only editable by an administrator.
Publicly accessible collection of technologies and skills the portfolio owner is proficient in, managed by the administrator.
Publicly accessible collection of portfolio projects, managed by the administrator.
Publicly accessible collection of professional certifications and achievements, managed by the administrator.
Publicly accessible collection of services offered by the portfolio owner, managed by the administrator.
Publicly accessible collection of visual assets for projects, profile pictures, certificates, and the admin-managed gallery. Includes denormalized 'category' for easy filtering and security rules.
Collection for client inquiries to hire services. Documents are only viewable and manageable by the portfolio administrator. Includes a 'status' field for workflow management.

params.name: inquiryId
params.description: Unique identifier for the hire me inquiry.

definition.description: Collection for inquiries from potential collaborators. Documents are only viewable and manageable by the portfolio administrator. Includes a 'status' field for workflow management.

params.name: inquiryId
params.description: Unique identifier for the collaboration inquiry.

definition.description: Collection for visitor comments and feedback. Publicly readable only if 'isApproved' is true. Administrators can create, read, update, delete all comments, and manage approval status using 'isApproved' and 'isSpam' fields.

Collection for users registered to access the chatBRJ feature. Document IDs ('chatUserId') match the user's Firebase Authentication UID. Users can read/update their own profile. Administrators can view all chat users.

params.name: chatUserId
params.description: The Firebase Authentication UID of the chat user.

definition.description: Collection for messages sent in the chatBRJ. Only authenticated chat users can create messages, and all authenticated users can read/list messages. Includes 'chatUserId' for sender attribution and authorization. Administrators can view all messages.

params.name: messageId
params.description: Unique identifier for the chat message.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. It prioritizes Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and consistent Access Modeling.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
*   **Inquiries and Comments:** `HireMeInquiry`, `CollaborationInquiry`, and `Comment` documents are self-contained. All necessary authorization context (e.g., `isApproved`, `status`) is embedded within each document. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to check parent documents or external data for authorization decisions, enabling atomic operations and simplifying rule logic.
*   **Chat Messages:** Each `ChatMessage` document includes `chatUserId`, explicitly identifying the sender. This allows rules to verify `request.auth.uid == resource.data.chatUserId` directly without fetching the `ChatUser` document.
*   **Admin Role:** Admin authentication relies on an 'existence over content' pattern. The `/roles_admin/{adminUid}` collection simply stores documents where the document ID is the administrator's Firebase Authentication UID. Rules check `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` for admin privileges, making it a highly independent and efficient check.

**Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
*   **Public Content:** Dedicated top-level collections like `/projects`, `/technologies`, `/certificates`, `/services`, and `/images` contain only publicly viewable data. This ensures all documents within these collections share the same broad 'publicly readable' security posture, simplifying rules to `allow read: true;` (with admin write access).
*   **Private Inquiries:** `inquiries_hire_me` and `inquiries_collaboration` are segregated collections containing sensitive inquiry data, accessible only to administrators, ensuring privacy.
*   **Comments:** The `/comments` collection holds all comments. While public users can only read `isApproved: true` comments, administrators have full read/write access. This allows content-based filtering for public `list` operations while maintaining a single management point for admins.
*   **Chat-Specific Data:** `chat_users` and `chat_messages` are distinct collections for the chat feature, ensuring authenticated access for chat users and full visibility for administrators.

**Access Modeling & QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
*   **Portfolio Owner Profile:** The `/user_profile/portfolioOwner` document is a single, static document that is publicly readable, but only writable by an administrator. This explicitly defines the 'owner' as the admin for management purposes.
*   **Public-facing Collections:** For `/projects`, `/technologies`, `/certificates`, `/services`, `/images`, the QAP is satisfied because rules generally allow `read, list: true;`. Any client-side filtering (e.g., by image `category`) does not impose authorization constraints from the rules perspective.
*   **Inquiries:** `inquiries_hire_me` and `inquiries_collaboration` enforce `allow read, list: isAdmin();`. This satisfies QAP as all documents in these collections are equally inaccessible to non-admins.
*   **Comments:** For public users, rules will typically enforce `allow read, list: if resource.data.isApproved == true;`. While this means rules act as a filter for `list` operations for public users, it's a widely accepted and practical pattern that clarifies intent: unapproved comments are explicitly hidden from the public. Admins, however, can list and read all comments without such filters, satisfying their requirement.
*   **Chat:** `chat_users/{chatUserId}` allows individual users to manage their own profile (`request.auth.uid == chatUserId`), while admins can list all. `chat_messages` allows all authenticated users to read/list all messages and create their own, while enforcing `request.auth.uid == request.resource.data.chatUserId` for message creation. This maintains homogeneity of access within the `chat_messages` collection for authenticated users.
